topic.title: Change-Point Detection and Nonstationary Prediction
topic.overview: Streaming data may change because the underlying process has shifted rather than because an unusual observation occurred. This topic studies detecting those changes and continuing to predict while their location is uncertain. Bayesian models, adaptive covariance structures, and sequential tests address different parts of the problem.
topic.whyItMatters: A detector must balance false alarms against delayed recognition, while a predictor may need to remain useful before a change is confidently identified. Computational cost also matters for long-running streams: a method that repeatedly revisits the entire history can become impractical even if its statistical behavior is attractive.
topic.evolution: A 1996 representative propagates probability samples through time for tracking. In 2009, Gaussian-process prediction explicitly integrates uncertainty about changepoints rather than treating detection as the only goal. Later work studies adaptive detectors and delay guarantees; a 2026 method handles dependent multivariate Poisson streams using low-rank intensity representations and constant per-observation computational cost.
openQuestions: How can gradual drift be separated from abrupt change and isolated outliers?
Which false-alarm guarantees remain meaningful under repeated adaptation to a live stream?
